purpose: Cut bounded subtractive features directly into observed existing rigid static UC GLB rectangular-prism meshes, including rotated stock, hash-linked cumulative notch chains, and hash-linked cumulative round-hole chains with exact prior-state reconstruction.

properties.source_path: existing ordinary .glb creation outside protected live machine body
properties.path: distinct target .glb path outside protected live machine body
properties.specification: closed v0.2 axis-aligned cut recipe, v0.3 oriented cut recipe, axm.mesh-fabrication-chain/v0.4 cumulative box-notch recipe, or axm.mesh-hole-fabrication-chain/v0.5 cumulative round-hole recipe
properties.expected_source_sha256: optional exact lowercase SHA-256 binding, with optional sha256: prefix
properties.lineage_path: v0.4/v0.5 optional prior lineage JSON receipt when appending to a previous chain output
properties.receipt_path: v0.4/v0.5 optional distinct output JSON receipt path; defaults beside the output GLB
properties.expected_lineage_sha256: v0.4/v0.5 optional exact prior lineage SHA-256 binding

contains: exact source GLB SHA-256 and source byte count
source closed edge-topology evidence before initial cutting
right-handed orthonormal source-frame axes and frame digest for rotated stock
cut recipe digests bound to exact source/frame state
hash-linked cumulative lineage with parent-to-child state hashes and final receipt digest
deterministic reconstruction of the prior cumulative output before any resume append
v0.5 stable inner hole polygons while slab seam tessellation is refined independently
v0.5 deterministic u/v slab partition evidence for supported multi-hole layouts
kerf-aware cut metrics and cumulative operation count
output closed edge-topology evidence before publication

relationships: reads actual existing GLB triangles through UC's static geometry decoder before calculating the first cut
reuses UC seam-weld topology evidence before and after fabrication
derives an orthonormal local frame from the observed eight stock corners instead of assuming world-axis alignment
binds an explicit world-space fabrication axis to exactly one proven source-frame axis
v0.4 preserves the proven source frame as lineage for cumulative non-overlapping box notches
v0.5 preserves the same proven frame for cumulative round holes and keeps each resolved hole polygon stable when new holes are appended
v0.5 synchronizes only outer slab seam events so adjacent slab triangulations weld without adding hidden material or reshaping earlier holes
v0.4/v0.5 verify prior receipt hashes, prior output digest and deterministic prior-output reconstruction before appending new operations
reuses the existing deterministic surface-to-GLB publisher and validator
keeps source bytes separate from the new output and refuses in-place cutting
limitations: v0.5 round-hole chaining is bounded to at most 32 non-overlapping/non-touching holes on one proven fabrication axis of one rigid rectangular-prism root stock.

v0.5 multi-hole layouts must be separable along one of the two canonical cross-section axes so synchronized deterministic slab seams can be proven. General polygon-with-holes triangulation remains unavailable.
v0.4 cumulative box-notch chains remain supported separately. Notch-and-hole mixing and cross-axis cumulative chains are still unavailable rather than approximated.
v0.3 single cuts still support round through-holes and box notches on rotated/transformed rectangular stock; arbitrary free-angle cutters relative to the proven stock frame remain rejected.
Multiple primitives/components, skins, animation, morphs, UVs, textures, tangents, vertex colours, joints and unsupported material state remain rejected rather than silently discarded.
Lineage receipts are content-hashed and exact-output-bound, but are not cryptographic authorship signatures or external trust anchors against coordinated replacement of both receipt and artifact.

General arbitrary-mesh boolean surgery remains unavailable. Edge-manifold topology is checked, but self-intersection, visual quality, structural strength, real manufacturing behavior and host-engine import are not proven.

truth.basis: Exact source bytes, source frame, cumulative recipes, stable per-hole digests, parent/child step hashes, deterministic prior-output reconstruction, topology, output digest, receipt digest and unsupported boundaries remain inspectable.

agency.basis: The caller chooses source, output, fabrication axis, hole locations/radii/resolution/kerf, resume receipt and replacement decision; unsupported overlap, mixed-operation, cross-axis and freeform requests fail closed.

continuity.basis: Source artifacts are read-only, resume receipts are append-only, prior output is deterministically reconstructed before continuation, earlier resolved hole boundaries stay stable, and output/receipt publication retains rollback behavior.

wisdom-before-speed.basis: The cutter proves initial stock topology/frame, validates every lineage hash and exact prior output on resume, rejects overlapping or unprovable layouts, synchronizes slab seams deterministically, then proves closed output topology and published GLB structure.
